reading.title: Reading a Character Like a Detective
reading.purpose: Use precise trait words to explain what a character's choices reveal.
paras: Authors rarely tell us everything about a character. Instead, they show a person acting, speaking, and choosing, and the reader must decide what those choices reveal. Learning precise words for character traits makes that thinking sharper.

Start with how a character faces risk. A cautious character checks the weather before a hike and packs extra water. An impulsive character leaps first and thinks later, sometimes with funny results and sometimes with trouble. Between them stands the reluctant character, who hesitates because the task is something he or she does not want to do.

Next, look at how a character treats the truth. A sincere speaker means every word, with nothing pretended. A candid speaker is honest and direct even when the answer is hard to hear, while a tactful speaker finds a kind way to say the same hard thing. Imagine a friend asking about a weak drawing. The candid reply is "It needs work," and the tactful reply is "The colors are great, and the faces might need more practice."

Some traits show up in how characters think. A perceptive character notices details that others miss, such as a nervous hand or a changed schedule. A skeptical character doubts a big claim until good evidence appears. Both traits help a character solve mysteries, and both are useful to readers too.

Finally, consider how characters handle effort and success. A persistent character keeps trying after the tenth failed attempt. A humble character, even after winning, remembers that there is still plenty left to learn. Readers usually admire these two traits because they last.
When you meet a new character, ask three questions. What does this person do? What does this person say? What would this person do next? Then choose the trait word that best fits the evidence.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, the word "candid" most nearly means
choices: careful to say hard things in a gentle way
willing to pretend to agree to avoid a quarrel
honest and direct about hard truths
unsure that any answer is really true
qs.why: The text says a candid speaker is "honest and direct even when the answer is hard to hear," unlike a tactful speaker, who softens the message.

qs.q: Which sentence shows what a cautious character does?
choices: A cautious character checks the weather before a hike and packs extra water.
An impulsive character leaps first and thinks later, sometimes with funny results and sometimes with trouble.
A persistent character keeps trying after the tenth failed attempt.
Start with how a character faces risk.
qs.why: Checking the weather and packing extra water are careful steps taken to avoid trouble.

ev.text: A cautious character checks the weather before a hike and packs extra water.

qs.q: Why would a perceptive and skeptical character make a good detective?
choices: Such a character acts quickly on every first idea.
Such a character notices small clues and wants good evidence.
Such a character avoids saying anything difficult to a suspect.
Such a character finds it easy to trust whatever people claim.
qs.why: A detective needs to notice details others miss (perceptive) and to doubt claims until there is evidence (skeptical).

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Most characters in stories can be described fully with just a single trait.
Authors should always tell readers exactly what each character is like.
Readers should judge a character only by what the other characters say.
Trait words help readers understand characters from their actions.
qs.why: Each paragraph pairs behavior with a trait word, and the last paragraph says to choose the word that fits the evidence.
